bars.name: Sea of Stars
bars.covers: Pixel art, animation, battle presentation, UI

bars.name: 60 fps
bars.covers: Measurable: frame budget on every build

pieces.name: Project, capture tools, references
pieces.note: Godot 4.7 project at 640x360, unattended screenshot and video capture, blind A/B tool, reference footage of all three games, master palette.

rounds.gap: Abilities get starved: 40% of heroes never fire their ability and 28% charge up then die unseen, because each hero waits about 7 s between turns. Super Auto Pets shows every promised trigger fire within seconds.

Sudden-death damage events break the documented event format and crash anything reading them (12% of fights). Formation effects are still invisible for 40% of sides, and abilities now fire so often they lose their punch.

Close. Every measured target passes now, but Backstab and Execute ignored the back-row halving (a spec rule with no exceptions), formation cues are too frequent and include effects under 10%, and some fights have long boring tails.
The last-unit sudden death made the arena the killer in a third of fights (now removed: sudden death is time-only, per the user). Backstab still bypassed the back-row halving under a new name.
Formation cues fired on units that weren't doing the named trigger in 54% of cases (a queue to show every effect made them lie). Fading, back-row rule and all targets now hold.

PASSED round 6: readability holds up against Super Auto Pets, and every target and spec rule is met (truthful cues, back row always half, time-only Fading, deterministic Echo replays, about 1.4-1.7 ms per fight).

pieces.name: Hero and monster sprites

rounds.gap: Sea of Stars won blind for both heroes and monsters. Our attacks only swing the weapon arm on a rigid body, idles are a 1-pixel bob, and KO poses look like the standing sprite rotated.

Sea of Stars won blind again on both pairs. Idles still freeze the legs and pelvis (the 1-pixel bob is now decorated with cloth flutter), attacks have no anticipation or lunge, and the Mage's head floats above the collar.

pieces.note: On hold: the user is deciding whether to refine or restyle the character and monster art. General look, encounters and UI are a solid start.

pieces.name: Encounter choice screen

rounds.gap: Ours won both blind pairs (the Weeping Colossus), but the other four encounters' illustrations read as placeholder art next to Slay the Spire, so the set as a whole loses.

Ours won 1 of 6 blind pairs (the Colossus). The Keeper, the hound, the girl and the old woman are still built from shaded shapes and read as placeholder art; they need hand-placed pixel figures. Text is also too small for a phone.

pieces.note: On hold: the user is deciding whether to refine or restyle the character and monster art. General look, encounters and UI are a solid start.

pieces.name: Battle scene presentation
pieces.bar: Sea of Stars + Super Auto Pets

rounds.gap: Sea of Stars won blind. The fight plays in a 110 px strip with 20 px units that overlap, squeezed between heavy HUD bands. Formation effects show only as tiny text, not on the board.
Won 1 of 3 blind pairs (beat a Super Auto Pets battle frame). Lost to Sea of Stars: too busy, no single focus, and the board sits too high so the top row and numbers clip into the HUD.

Won 1 of 4 blind pairs. Old damage numbers pile up across actions, the big starburst came back on heavy hits, and formation effects still read as small floating text rather than something on the board.

Won 1 of 4 blind pairs. Damage numbers still outlive their action and drift from their targets, the Fading shows for only about 3 s before turning into a plain label, and abilities feel big only in the bottom panel.
Won 1 of 4 blind pairs. Damage numbers float far above their targets (likely a camera-zoom coordinate bug), and the Fading lasts only 2 s in the demo before leaving a stray label over VICTORY.

Close: won 3 of 5 blind pairs, including the Fading frame, but lost 2 of 3 against real Sea of Stars combat. Back-row attackers barely move, so you can't tell who hit whom without the caption, and the enemy side is crowded.

Lost all 3 pairs against real Sea of Stars combat frames (won 2 against idle Super Auto Pets frames). Spec holds and the earlier fixes landed, but the board has no spectacle: eight small, similarly lit units, and ability effects only a few pixels across.

Won 3 of 5 blind pairs (beat Sea of Stars once, both Super Auto Pets frames) but lost 2 of 3 against Sea of Stars. 10 of 16 formation behaviours read clearly; 6 are only text tags. The healed ally is still dimmed in Mend.
Won 3 of 5 blind pairs; 12 of 16 shapes read. Lost 2 of 3 Sea of Stars pairs because area-ability moments turn into white soup or near-black darkness, with numbers piling up.

pieces.note: Round-9 fixes mostly in (no white-out, one number per target, brightness floor, icon cap). Not yet re-judged; a few collisions are still unaddressed.

pieces.name: Alignment grid and memories UI

rounds.gap: Sea of Stars won both blind pairs. Our screen is a dense wall of small text across four panels; the grid needs to dominate and the legend needs to shrink to one detail line.

pieces.note: On hold: the user is deciding whether to refine or restyle the character and monster art. General look, encounters and UI are a solid start.

pieces.name: Hero draft and formation setup screens
pieces.bar: Super Auto Pets team screen + Sea of Stars menus

rounds.gap: Soft pass not counted: both wins came against weak Super Auto Pets frames. Lost to the Sea of Stars menu on density; the formation panel is a wall of small text, and list portraits don't match the grid sprites.
Lost all 4 blind pairs against clean Super Auto Pets and Sea of Stars frames: still three equal-weight text columns. Restructuring to one grid plus one shape card, with a slim portrait tray.

Won 1 of 4 blind pairs: the draft screen beat Super Auto Pets. The formation card still loses to Sea of Stars on polish: dead space, faint locked rows, a tooltip covering the next line, and ghost labels cluttering the board.

Won 2 of 4 blind pairs, both against Super Auto Pets; lost both Sea of Stars pairs. The Strays card has labels over 20 characters and contradicts itself, the locked fallback headlines the wrong shape, and the card's rhythm is too busy.

Won 2 of 4 blind pairs, including the first win over a Sea of Stars menu (the draft screen). The formation board still loses: sprites overlap their neighbours while 40% of the board is empty, and some text is too small for a phone.

pieces.note: Hero draft and formation setup: drag or tap onto the 2x4 grid, live shape naming with bonus, behaviour, cost and growth path, locked shapes shown as Strays, opponent formation hidden.

pieces.name: Run loop core: hidden map, encounters, phases, Echo PvP, rewards
pieces.bar: Slay the Spire run flow + spec

rounds.gap: The legend gate doesn't follow the user's design yet, the opponent's formation leaks before the fight, 89% of runs repeat encounters (only 20 exist), and the run has no arc: PvP is a flat coin flip with no mid-run spikes.

PASSED round 2: every spec rule and user decision holds. The run has a real arc (health drains floor by floor, deaths spread over floors 3-5), choices always change what comes next, and runs differ. Polish follow-ups: give guardians an identity, more distinct rival names.

pieces.note: Built: hidden map (29 nodes), phases, memories, Echo PvP against a saved pool, health, rewards, pluggable Legend gate, a bot that plays 200 runs. 77 tests pass. Critic waits until the party-size and formation design is settled.

pieces.name: Formation redesign: distinct per-shape effects

rounds.gap: Close: detection perfect across 210 placements and every cue truthful. Small fixes: Strays cancelled splash even between adjacent units, Keeper's Ring slightly weak (38.8%), monster ability share 24%, one ring check missing, two cue wordings.
PASSED round 2: 210 placements detected perfectly, every behaviour checked against its geometry, 0 of 6976 cues untruthful, all 16 shapes between 43% and 56%, all earlier combat targets hold.

pieces.note: Approved design (05-formations.md): 15 lore-named shapes growing from dominoes to tetrominoes, Strays, Training Grounds unlocks (locked shapes fight as Strays). Combat-core builder implementing.

pieces.name: Team name, crest and PvP splash screen
pieces.note: User idea: players name their team and customise a crest (unlocked through Lanternrest, likely the Banner Hall), shown on a splash screen before PvP battles.

pieces.name: Crystal of Remembrance (final chamber)
pieces.note: Built end to end: the combat sim, the run's final node, and the battle presentation (a large crystal with an integrity bar and fragment pips, memories surfacing with lore captions, the Shard breaking free). Not yet critic-judged.

pieces.name: High-resolution UI text layer
pieces.bar: Sea of Stars menus, Super Auto Pets shop

rounds.gap: FAIL round 1: ours 2/5 blind pairs (won both Super Auto Pets pairs, lost all three Sea of Stars menu pairs); open review FAIL. Biggest gap: thin, dim secondary text (2.5-3.9:1) fades at phone size, and the finer text reclaimed no space, so screens are no calmer. Also: overlaps on the setup drag preview and the hero-detail plates. Fix list: docs/tasks/hires-ui-round1.md.

pieces.note: World stays 640x360 pixel art; UI text and chrome on a native-resolution layer with new pixel-styled fonts (x-height >= 14 px at 1080p), aspect expand, full-resolution captures. Round 1 FAILED (2/5). Round-2 fixes NOT started: see docs/tasks/hires-ui-round1.md (open question for the user on intro cards / Details first).

log.msg: Project set up: Godot 4.7 at 640x360, capture tools, blind A/B tool, master palette, reference footage of all three bars.
Wave 1 starting: combat core, hero sprites, encounter screen.
Hero sprites builder started.
Encounter screen builder started.
Reference footage expanded: Sea of Stars town and menus, real Slay the Spire event screens (replaced a board-game clip downloaded by mistake).
Combat core built: 50 tests pass, 0.86 ms per fight, median fight 24.6 s, no stalemates. Critic round 1 started.
Combat core round 1: critic FAILED it. All measurements held, but abilities often never fire on screen. Sent back to the builder.
Paused: usage cap reached. Resuming after 9:20pm ET.
Resumed after the usage reset: combat core fixes, hero sprites and encounter screen builders all continuing.
Encounter screen built (five illustrated encounters, shared UI theme and original pixel fonts). Critic round 1 judging blind.
Wave 2 started early: alignment grid and hero detail screen builder running.
Hero sprites built: 4 heroes and 3 Vault monsters with full animation sets. Showcase being re-laid out on the spec's 2x4 formation grid before its critic round.
Spec non-negotiables added to the build guide (2-column x 4-row formation per side, visible formation buffs). Every critic now fails a piece that breaks them.
Encounter screen round 1: critic picked ours blind on both pairs, but FAILED the piece. Only the Colossus holds up and the other four illustrations need to match it. Sent back to the builder.

Combat core round 2 fixes in: 93% of heroes now fire their ability (was 60%), 4.2 s between turns, formation effects signed and visible, Echo validation hardened. 58 tests pass. Critic round 2 started.
Battle scene builder started: FF1-style side view, 2-column x 4-row grid per side, formation banner with buff and debuff, playback of the combat log.
Sprite showcase re-laid out on the 2x4 formation grid per side. Hero sprites critic round 1 started (blind vs Sea of Stars, at matched pixel scale).
Hero sprites round 1: Sea of Stars won blind on heroes and monsters. Key poses being redrawn as whole-body drawings; showcase becomes a labelled gallery.
Combat core round 2: FAILED. Round-1 targets all pass, but sudden-death events crash readers, many formation effects are still invisible, and abilities are now too frequent. Sent back.
Encounter screen round 2 built: all four weaker illustrations redone, art reacts to outcomes, recruits join, advancement shown before the pick. Critic round 2 judging six blind pairs.
Night mode: no new pieces will start. Pieces already running continue their loops until done or until the usage cap.
Encounter screen round 2: ours won 1 of 6 blind pairs. Figures are being repainted as hand-placed pixel art, and text enlarged for phones.

Hero sprites round 2 built: whole-body key poses, 12-frame idles with cloth and hair motion, collapsed KO poses, hit recoil, new monster faces. Showcase is now a labelled gallery. Critic round 2 judging.
Alignment screen built and in critic round 1. Blind comparison tool fixed so small game captures and full-HD references are scaled the same way.
Hero sprites round 2: Sea of Stars won blind again. Key poses now being hand-placed as full-body pixel maps, with pixel-measured pass checks for idle and attack motion.

Combat core round 3 fixes in: crash fixed with a full event-format test, formation effects shown for every formation, abilities 27% of actions (was 43%), Echo loader hardened. 65 tests pass. Critic round 3 started.
Alignment screen round 1: Sea of Stars won both blind pairs (too dense, grid not dominant). Sent back. Open question for the user logged: the Fighter's starting alignment.
Paused at 93% of the session limit. All agents stopped cleanly; resume notes updated.
Resumed with a small budget, closing existing loops only: combat core critic round 3 and battle scene critic round 1 running. Sprites, encounter art and alignment screen reworks are on hold.
Battle scene round 1: FAILED (fight too small on screen, formation effects only as tiny text). Spec layout confirmed. Sent back to the builder.
Combat core round 3: FAILED but close. All measurements pass; remaining: remove the back-row exception, trim formation cues, shorten boring tails. Sent back.
Battle scene round 2 built: 2x camera so units are about 80 px tall, formation effects light up the grid tiles, hit-stop and ability flashes, short victory hold. Critic round 2 judging.
Battle scene round 2: won 1 of 3 blind pairs (beat Super Auto Pets). Still loses to Sea of Stars on focus and clipping. Round 3 fixes underway.
Combat core round 4 fixes in: back-row rule restored for every hit, formation cues down to about 3 per fight (all 10% or more), long tails 2.7% (was 10-15%). 67 tests pass. Critic round 4 started.
Battle scene round 3 built: board lowered with a centre gap, focus dimming on non-acting units, big formation badges, smaller hit sparks, no READY clutter. Critic round 3 judging four blind pairs.
Battle scene round 3: won 1 of 4 blind pairs. Popups now limited to the current action, flashes capped, formation effects to be shown on the board. Round 4 underway.

Combat core round 4: FAILED. Your call confirmed: the last-unit trigger made sudden death decide a third of fights. Now time-based only and themed as the Fading. Backstab's back-row bypass removed for real.

Battle scene round 4 built: popups cleared per action, small hit sparks only, on-board formation tile fills, ability beats, and sudden death presented as the Fading (the arena drains to grey). Critic round 4 judging.
Battle scene round 4: won 1 of 4 blind pairs. Stale numbers not actually fixed; the builder must now self-verify with contact sheets before reporting.

Combat core round 5 fixes in: sudden death is time-based only and called the Fading (a tick decides the last KO in 5.8% of fights, was 32%), back-row halving applies to every hit, every formation effect shows once per fight. 68 tests pass. Critic round 5 waits for the next session.
Battle scene round 5 fixes in (popups pinned to their targets, deeper Fading, ability moments on the board). Critic round 5 waits for the next session. All agents idle.
New session: combat core critic round 5 and battle scene critic round 5 running.

Battle scene round 5: 1 of 4 blind wins. Lead diagnosed the floating numbers as a camera-zoom coordinate bug; the builder must verify on screen pixels this time. The Fading needs to run 8 s or more in the demo.
Combat core round 5: FAILED on formation cues naming the wrong unit (54%). Rule now: cues only when true; uncued effects shown in the fight-start banner. Everything else holds.

Battle scene round 6 built: numbers anchored on their targets (the real cause was the anchor point, not the camera), the Fading runs about 10 s in the PvP demo and clears on VICTORY. Critic round 6 judging five blind pairs.
Combat core round 6 fixes in: formation cues are now always truthful (0 of 4141 mismatched, was 54%), back-row labels name attacker or target, Fading wording in the narration. Critic round 6 started.
Battle scene round 6: best yet, won 3 of 5 blind pairs (incl. the Fading frame). Fixes confirmed for numbers and the Fading. Remaining: attacker travel, crowding, caption gaps.
Combat core PASSED (critic round 6). First piece to beat its bar. Minor polish items logged for the formation redesign.

Battle scene round 7 built: attackers visibly travel or fire projectiles, no edge clipping, Sentinel given room, formation glints on hits. Critic round 7 judging five blind pairs against real combat frames only.
Battle scene round 7: lost all 3 pairs against real Sea of Stars combat. Spec and earlier fixes hold; gap is spectacle (ability effects too small, no single focus). Paused for the user's direction.
Checkpoint committed on branch gauntlet-build and tagged checkpoint-pre-spectacle. Battle round 8 started as a switchable spectacle experiment for the user to approve.
New direction from the user: mechanics and a playable vertical slice before art polish. Spectacle level 2 is the default and will become a Battle Effects setting. Run loop core builder started.
Run loop core built: 29-node hidden map, phases, Echo PvP, health, rewards, pluggable Legend gate. 77 tests pass. Critic held until the party-size and formation design is settled.
Formation design drafted for the user (05-formations-draft.md): shapes grow from dominoes to tetrominoes, each with a bonus, a behaviour and a cost. Legendary uses a rising chance.
Formation draft updated with the user's answers: lore names (Kindred, Tidebreak, Seawall, Lighthouse, Keeper's Ring...), Strays for loose ranks, Training Grounds drills, opponent formations hidden.
Formation design approved as 05-formations.md. Training Grounds unlocks formation bonuses; drills dropped. Formation build started in the combat core.
API overload passed (health check OK, status page all operational). Formation build restarted.

Formation redesign built: 15 shapes plus Strays, all within 41-58% win rate, 87 tests pass, every cue truthful. User approved the rebalance and two behaviour changes (Keeper's Ring full protection, Lighthouse draws casters); builder applying them.

Formation changes applied: Keeper's Ring now fires in 32 of 100 fights (was 3), the Lighthouse taunt in 39 (was 7); all shapes 41-57%; run layer passes unlocks; 89 tests pass. Formation critic round 1 started.
More capacity: four agents in parallel. Formation critic, run loop critic, hero draft and formation setup screens builder, and battle scene update for the new formations.
Run loop round 1: FAILED. Spec fixes sent back (legend gate, hidden opponent formation, 60+ encounters with no repeats, meaningful routing). Run arc and alignment steering are questions for the user.
User decisions for runs: floor guardians plus rest encounters, PvP matched by floor, about 1 in 4 encounters let a hero steer between two directions. Sent to the run builder.
Battle scene updated for the new formations: lore banner, an on-board moment for every behaviour, Hold the door step-forward, 16 per-shape clips. Critic round 8 judging.
Formation round 1: FAILED but close (detection perfect, cues truthful). Small fixes sent back to the combat builder.
Battle round 8: 3 of 5 blind wins; 10 of 16 formation behaviours read clearly. Round 9: on-board visuals for the other 6, a proper Mend fix, less text clutter, rim light on focused units.
Hero draft and formation setup screens built. Critic round 1 judging against Super Auto Pets' team screen and Sea of Stars menus.
Setup screens round 1: critic passed it, but both wins were against weak reference frames, so it's not counted. Sent back: calmer panel hierarchy, matching portraits, labelled stats.

Checkpoint committed. Run loop round 2 fixes in (5 floors with guardians, 65 encounters with no repeats, PvP by floor, rising legend chance); critic round 2 started. User idea queued: team name, crest and PvP splash screen.
Setup screens round 2: calm glance panel with details behind a button, matching portraits, labelled stats, concrete costs. Critic round 2 judging against clean reference frames.
Setup screens round 2: lost all 4 blind pairs (too busy). Round 3 restructures to one grid plus one shape card.
Formation round 2 fixes in: Strays splash rule corrected, Keeper's Ring 43%, monster ability share 26%, all shapes 43-56%. Critic round 2 started.
Run loop PASSED (critic round 2), the second piece to beat its bar. Committed. Polish pass running: guardian identities, distinct rival names.
User idea adopted: formation effects as icons (stat icon plus green or red arrow, a glyph per behaviour) with tooltips on hover or tap. One shared component for the setup screen and battle banner.
User design: the final chamber becomes the Crystal of Remembrance (chip 4 fragments to free a Shard while story memories surface). Spec 06 written; combat core build started.
Run polish committed: named, escalating floor guardians, distinct rival team names, crest fields on Echoes. Run builder briefed to integrate the Crystal once the combat core has it.

Setup screens round 3: grid-first layout, slim bench, one shape card with icon plus short label lines (user's choice), shared effect icons and tooltip built. Critic round 3 judging. Battle banner switching to icons.
Formation redesign PASSED (critic round 2): the third piece to beat its bar. Small follow-ups logged for after the Crystal build.
Setup screens round 3: the draft screen won its blind pair; the formation card still loses to Sea of Stars on polish. Round 4 underway.

User decision: Strays now means truly spread out (no two side by side) and is its own formation; partly connected = Unformed; a locked shape falls back to its largest unlocked smaller shape. Spec updated; core change queued after the Crystal.
Setup screens show the new Strays, Unformed and locked-fallback states (a locked Crescent fights as Tidebreak, with the active heroes lit). Core implementation queued after the Crystal.
Battle banner switched to your icons: each effect a chip with a tooltip, and the chip pulses when its behaviour fires. Tooltip duplicate-title bug sent to the shared component's owner.
Tooltip fixed. Battle critic round 9 and setup screens critic round 4 running in parallel.
Crystal of Remembrance built in the combat core and committed. Now in parallel: run layer makes it the final node, battle scene presents it, core adds the Strays/Unformed/locked-fallback rule.
Setup screens round 4: 2 of 4 blind wins (both vs Super Auto Pets). Round 5: Strays wording, fighting shape as headline, calmer card rhythm.
Battle round 9: 3 of 5 blind wins, 12 of 16 shapes read. Next: no white-out or full-screen colour, a brightness floor on dimming, one number per target. Queued after the Crystal presentation.
Session at 60% of the plan limit: running builders finish, no new builders this session, limited critics, wrap up cleanly by 85%.
Setup screens round 5: 2 of 4 blind wins, including the first win over a Sea of Stars menu (draft). Remaining fixes (crowded board, tiny text) queued for next session per the budget plan.
Core now implements Strays/Unformed/locked fallback, matching the setup screen exactly (parity test). Shapes 40-58%. Committed.
Crystal of Remembrance is now the final node of every run (committed). Greedy victory 21%; Crystal won 58% when reached.
Crystal battle presentation and round-9 fixes committed. Session wrapped up at ~80% of the plan; next steps in the resume notes.

hires-ui round 2 built (4a08adb, 133 tests); critic round 2 started on captures/hires-ui/r2 with 2340x1080 phone pairs.

hires-ui round-3 build (local): numbers on their own head (legacy world-px band clamps removed; BattleFX.number_anchor tested), two-line crystal caption, setup tips in the panel, encounter wide backdrop, calmer draft/encounter/hero detail (ability short label + tooltip), 48 px hit areas, cue plates, hound capture. Captures captures/hires-ui/r3/; awaiting critic round 3.
hires-ui round 3 built (f4afbce, 150 tests; numbers anchored to sprite tops with a tested anchor function). Critic round 3 started.
hires-ui critic round 3: FAIL, 0/5 overall but 3/5 at phone size; legibility, floors and rules all pass; fails on 4 overlaps and calm/hierarchy (dense screens, weak primary buttons).

hires-ui round-4 build: capture tooling for scaled monitors, r3 overlaps fixed, caption sync, amber primary buttons, calmer encounter/hero detail/draft/setup; captures in captures/hires-ui/r4 and captures/flow/r4; critic round 4 next
hires-ui critic round 4: FAIL, 2/5 (SAP pairs won, SoS lost on density). Open review: Lanternrest label clip, splash contrast, Crystal banner timing.

questions: Fighter starting alignment: it starts at (0,+1) on the neutral axis, so it has no single super-rare far corner as the spec describes. Starting positions are an open question in the spec. Pick a start for the Fighter (e.g. off-axis), or accept two equally rare far corners.
